newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Two Arabs in Israeli court in land dealer's death.
newsitem.headline: Two Arabs in Israeli court in land dealer's death.

text.p: An Israeli court on Thursday ordered the detention of a Palestinian man and a woman on suspicion of involvement in the murder of an Arab alleged by Israel to have been killed for selling land to Jews.
Israeli police identified the man as a Palestinian police officer.

Asked if Israel believed he killed 70-year-old Farid Bashiti last week at the behest of Palestinian authorities, a police spokeswoman said the Jerusalem court had banned publication of any details of the investigation.
Bashiti's death followed a Palestinian Authority decision to apply the death penalty against Arabs convicted of selling land to Israelis.
The 33-year-old woman who was brought to court met Bashiti at an East Jerusalem hotel hours before his body was found in the Palestinian-ruled West Bank town of Ramallah, police said.
Israel's Foreign Ministry said on Wednesday that Bashiti, an East Jerusalem resident with Israeli citizenship, appeared to have been lured or forcibly abducted from Jerusalem to Ramallah.

Israel Radio called the woman suspect, who fainted in court, the Palestinian "Cindy", after a Mossad agent who in 1986 lured Israeli nuclear technician Mordechai Vanunu from London to Rome, where he was abducted and brought to Israel to stand trial for leaking atomic secrets to Britain's Sunday Times.
"This murder should be viewed within the context of a recent Palestinian Council decision invoking the death penalty against anyone who sells land to Jews," the Foreign Ministry said in a statement.
Bashiti's family said they believed his death was related to a personal dispute with someone. It did not name the person.
Police said the court ordered the male suspect detained for seven days and the woman for eight.
"They are suspected of involvement in the murder of Farid al-Bashiti," the spokeswoman said.
Palestinian security sources had said that Bashiti was killed by a blow with a sharp object to the head. They denied any links to his death.

The PLO says Israelis have been purchasing land in the West Bank, including Arab East Jerusalem, to block a political agreement which the PLO hopes would end Israeli rule in the areas captured by the Jewish state in the 1967 Middle East war.
PLO-appointed clergymen in Jerusalem, citing a religous ruling, have refused to pray over Bashiti's body or allow him to be buried in a Moslem cemetery.
Israel tried to bury the body in Jaffa, a former Arab town in Israel which is now part of Tel Aviv, but they were met with opposition from local residents.
